Yeah, I was kinda on fire and mega motivated in August. Was then pretty busy elsewhere in September, which was natural in the sense that I saw it coming, so I was fine with it. While in October came the unexpected dark times. So a variety of circumstances led to this draught of mine. But yeah, realistically speaking, it takes much to turn me off this way. Yet it would take fairly little to light up my mood again. Like some leaked blurry January would do the trick, but they seem to be some way off. So I remain hopeful for the remainder of the year that actually getting to build something new and finally add some new minifigs on the plate will reignite my enthusiasm for the theme. I know, I want to. It just needs to happen again.

posts.title: Armada treasure ship 'Fortuna' - MOD of set 31387 - real world model with backstory
posts.text: In August 1579, while on the way across the the Pacific Ocean enroute back to England after a round-the-world journey, Francis Drake came across a small longboat carrying a half-dead foreign sailor with a tale to tell. Before expiring, he imparted his knowledge to Captain Drake. His story was secreted away in the British royal archives for many centuries, as it was so fantastic as to be nearly unbelievable. The following is what the sailor said: Sailing to the West Indies in late 1566, the Armada vessel Fortuna lost it's way and ended up in a heavy fog. It eventually came to rest in a bay of an island not shown on any maps. This island was populated by strange giant reptiles, an active volcano, and the ancient ruins of a lost civilization. When the sun broke through the clouds, it was revealed the ruins were practically built from gold! It was also noticed that time behaved strangely on the island - as it it was practically standing still compared to the world at large. This was discovered when a fishing expedition came back after only a few hours saying they had been lost in the fog for about two days! The crew and officers were divided on what to do - some wanted to fill the hold with gold and make a beeline straight for home in Spain, but others wanted to start a kingdom of their own - pirating passing ships and creating a paradise. This culminated in a battle between the two factions, and the death of enough men to make a voyage anywhere impossible in the Fortuna. The surviving few men and officers decided to send out a small crew of the most able-bodied sailors out with a longboat to find help - no matter the nationality of the vessel. Fate was not kind to these men, as they had no idea where they were in the pacific anyway: after getting lost in the fog again, most of them men died of lack of supplies and diseases. Drifting aimlessly, the last two men drew straws - the winner would survive with the remaining supplies, and the loser would get the pistol and a quick burial at sea. It wasn't long after the winner was drawn and the gun gone off that Drake sailed into the horizon. Finishing his tale, the Sailor asked what year it was: when it was said it was 1579, he replied it only seemed like 6 months on the island when in reality 13 years had gone by. The shock of this revelation proved to be too much for the sailor, and he died shortly thereafter, with his body given to the sea, but not before marking the spot on the map where the island most likely was. Drake and his officers agreed it was not a good idea to go to this island, as it just wasn't worth the risks. Fast forward to 1923 when Johnny Thunder and his friends rediscover the long-forgotten island, and names it Dino Island, after it's ancient reptilian inhabitants. He doesn't explore it fully as he has his hands full dealing with Lord Sam Sinister and his cronies, so he missed the ancient ruins and the old shipwreck of the Fortuna, laden with gold. But, as Pippen Reed has recently gone missing on the island while making a documentary film, it seems that a return to Dino Island in 1926 is imminent! Will the treasure ship be found and the gold recovered? Only time will tell! Ok, so I've had this treasure ship model finished for a number of months and I just yesterday finally got around to taking pictures of it. The vessel is a modified copy of set 31387 - Iconic Pirate Ship. I took away the pirate-y stuff, added a black falcon figurehead, redid the sails a bit, and added a old armada flag from the 1990's. The custom cannons are also new, while the kit-bashed crew has been assembled since 2024. The stern (rear) of the ship. Here's the gun deck. I was disappointed to see in the new Creator set 31387 - Iconic Pirate Ship that only two cannons are provided, and that four firing cannons being installed at the same time is impossible. posts.text: Given the frequent stock issues of color variations I’d love to see sellers introduce a backorder service. Imagine being able to place and pay for an order upfront - even if some parts are currently out of stock - and having the seller automatically fulfill and ship the complete order once everything is restocked. Upfront payments would ensure buyers are committed, so sellers don't have to worry about cancelled orders or wasted storage space. This seems like a true win-win (at least to me): For Customers: We get to place a single order without constantly checking for restocks, knowing it will ship in one complete package once ready. For Sellers: Higher order volume, guaranteed sales, and predictable demand for restocks. Would anyone else find a feature like this useful or is it just me?!

posts.title: Adventurers on Holiday: a Short Story in Pictures
posts.text: Thank you! And now the conclusion. Johnny peered into the moonlight. As the colonel had predicted, an enormous hyena crept toward the oblivious sheep. Stopping suddenly, it sniffed the air and looked straight at the hunters' hiding spot before letting out a laugh that sounded uncannily human. With surprising speed for a beast of its size, the creature sprinted towards the two men. "What's the plan?" Colonel Smythe asked, fumbling to cock his revolver. "This!" Johnny replied. He jumped up and charged at the beast, firing wildly as he ran. Not expecting its intended victims to fight back, the fisi veered sharply off course and leapt over the fence of the nearby churchyard. Johnny and the colonel, their ears still ringing from the gunfire, could barely hear the sound of a tombstone shattering under the creature's weight. They ran nearly all the way around the churchyard in their frantic search for the gate. Both men held their weapons at the ready as they searched among the graves for their prey. "Look!" Colonel Smythe shouted. "There he is!" Johnny advanced cautiously. There, its head resting pitifully on the remnants of a broken monument, lay the motionless fisi. The vicar, followed by the local constable, soon joined Johnny and the colonel. "What in blazes is all this commotion?" the vicar demanded. "Colonel Smythe, don't tell me you're still on about all this were-hyena rubbish! Oh...oh, I see." "Are you sure it's dead?" said the constable. "It isn't moving, but I don't see any blood." "I'm pretty sure," said Johnny. "Wait! Something's happening!" Before their eyes, the fisi changed from a hyena to a lifeless man in an old-fashioned army uniform. "Major Pierce!" Colonel Smythe exclaimed. "I arrested him in Rhodesia because of his brutality to the natives, but he disappeared before the court-martial could be held. We'd always suspected him of dabbling in bush magic." "He must have hated you all this time," said Johnny, "And followed you back to England." "None of your shots hit him," said the constable after examining the body, "So how did he die?" "When he jumped the fence," the vicar observed, "He landed on consecrated ground. That's not good for a witch." "And I didn't get a single picture," Pippin, who had arrived too late to photograph the transformation, lamented. While Colonel Smythe left to help the constable bury the major elsewhere, Johnny and Pippin stayed behind to chat with the vicar. The sun was rising as Dr. Kilroy strode down the path toward the church. "Ah, I'm glad I found you," he said. "I've spent all night doing research, and I've got a hypothesis that may explain what happened to those sheep without resorting to the colonel's fanciful speculations. I say, isn't this the old Norman church I told you about? You've been examining that inscription without me!" "Oh no," said Johnny, "The vicar was just telling us about a village a few miles from here that may have been the site of Camelot. If we hurry we can catch the next train there." The End

posts.title: LEGO Star Wars Set Discussion 2026 - READ FIRST POST!!!
posts.text: Mercenaries would be my bet too. After how well the initial setup of the First Order was done in the novels and comics (Imperial Remnants and offshoots hiding out in the Unknown Regions eventually coalescing into a military junta), only for them to conveniently be bolstered by Palpatine’s Final Order (also in the Unknown Regions) and then all wiped out fairly quickly at the end of TRoS, the next major antagonistic force in the galaxy needs to be well-thought out. I absolutely do not want to get a retread with a First Order Remnant. I still chuckle at Finn’s ‘people are rising up all over the galaxy line’. To this day I feel like TRoS really could have used a montage-style ending like Return of the King to truly feel final. Although of course, that is no longer the case. Alas I regret to inform you that the Xyston which took a day trip out to Kijimi did indeed return to Exegol before the big battle - it’s in the film’s extended novelisation. I agree in principle though, it feels unrealistic for the First Order to be taken down so quickly even after the defeat at Exegol. Honestly as consumer-centric as this sentiment is, but I hope the enemy faction in the film is something brand new, if only to get some awesome new helmeted character / trooper design. It’s an area Star Wars has never failed to excel at, and will doubtless make for good minifigure potential. I don’t expect this level of nuance in the show (and I say this as a fan of its story), but it’ll be interesting to see how the Thrawn campaign in Ahsoka S2 and its catastrophic effects on the New Republic will feed into Mon Mothma’s Disarmament Act. I still have mixed feelings on her decision particularly as it ripened the galaxy at large for the First Order to take over so quickly. On that note - I highly recommend reading The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire by Chris Kempshall. It’s a fantastic read that touches on a lot of this. I completely feel you man, haven’t seen you around in quite a bit. I’m hoping that once some images for next year’s sets start trickling out that it’ll incite some excitement in all of us, but I also feel bummed out around some of the asinine decisions they’re making with this theme. Brilliant, brilliant. I’m also imagining the scene from GotG Vol. 2 where Groot is instructed to bring back Yondu’s fin but keeps bringing back other worthless knick-knacks too. Conscious this post mostly isn’t about Lego, I genuinely want to understand some of the decision-making behind this theme. I really struggle to see how Lucasfilm put out so many of these toyetic shows and the Lego Star Wars team gladly overlook them entirely. Are they burned out based on the sales data? Do they simply think people aren’t interested in these shows? I struggle to think that they wouldn’t be aware of how toy-friendly these shows are. But maybe the corporate decision-makers truly are that out of touch. And that weird sense of priorities spills over into other things too. Sets like Bounty Hunter Pursuit and Ewok Village have been requested repeatedly for years. To think these sets were indeed planned and then either delayed or cancelled (again) during the 50th Anniversary year of Star Wars just makes so little sense to me. I’m all for trying new things, but it genuinely perplexes me that we’re getting two Marvel crossover sets instead of these. There’s obviously a lot of factors that go into the number of sets they produce per year, but I wish they could have found a way to release BHP and Ewok Village next year. I guess Hasbro’s recent reveal of Zam Wessel in the Black Series has resurfaced my annoyance at how poor Lego Star Wars’ coverage of the saga is as of late.

posts.title: [MOC] Frauenkirche Dresden
posts.text: Hello again, I built two prototypes of the lantern arcades: The yellow model with roof and cross was used to find the right proportions. The white one includes the details of the columns and arches. From the virtual tour, I obtained the following dimensions for the arcades: - clear distance between the columns: 3,51 m / 54 = 6,5 cm (8 studs) - clear height from the visitors platform floor level to the top of the arches: 8,59 m / 54 = 15,9 cm (16 bricks) The stonework of the Frauenkirche ends at an elevation of 78,03 m / 54 = 144,5 cm In the MOC this corresponds to the distance from the red 2x2 plate (street level) to the measuring rod, which is 145,4 cm. This means an error of approx. one brick’s height. With shorter columns the arcades would lose their proportions and the arches with their cornice are already as flat as they can be. After some close fight, my inner Monk and I agreed to leave the lantern as it is . The capitals of the columns were raised by 1/5 of a stud width (red = before / green = after). The small gap towards the cornice above disappeared and the columns could be tiled without any gaps. With this puzzle finished, the columns could be built at last. Each brick column stands on just one stud. This fragile structure will not be stable, before the arches are inserted. The stair case cylinder gives some additional stability. The light-weight lantern with its big roof must withstand high wind loads. The column stones with boreholes are threaded onto tension rods, which attach the columns firmly to the lantern base. Transverse and diagonal tension rods at the imposts of the arches stiffen the structure and compensate the shear force from the stone-built arches. In my model I used rigid hoses as horizontal tension rods. These fit firmly into the rings of the plates 41632 and further stabilize the structure. The provisional frame of 1x10 bricks and 6x6 plates helps to position the rigid hoses. Each three brick columns are firmly combined with facet bricks 2462. Arches with supporting structure for the surrounding narrow ridge: The capitals on top of the columns are just laid in loosely. A short technic pin holds the inside tile in place. Thanks to this smooth surface without studs, the tiles can be set into the corners without tension. No glue was used! Later, this tricky solution will not be visible. The spiral stairs lead to the lantern roof. The wooden ceiling is built with long tiles and cheese slopes and inserted upside down. The roof cornice is covered with copper sheets. The half arches 3572 are not (yet) available in dark stone grey, my color selection for weathered copper surfaces. Plates on top of the lantern ceiling make a firm base for the roof. See you soon. Greetings, Justus

posts.title: Privateer Frigate Fortuna LEGO 910059-1 (Stud.io Digital Recreation)
posts.text: Hello everyone! After spending some time away from digital LEGO building, I recently decided to give BrickLink Stud.io a try. In the past,I used to build quite a few digital models in LEGO Digital Designer (LDD), so it has been fun getting back into digital building with new software. For my first Stud.io project, I decided to recreate Privateer Fortuna, the beautiful ship designed by Brickperfection for the BrickLink Designer Program Series 7. This is a digital recreation of the original design, made for my own enjoyment and to explore the possibilities of Stud.io. All credit for the original design belongs to its creator. With the designer's blessing, I'm happy to share the Stud.io file with the Eurobricks community for anyone interested in taking a closer look at the model. Original BrickLink Designer Program project: BrickLink: Privateer Frigate Fortuna BDP Series 7 Digital model: Privateer Frigate Fortuna (Stud.io file) A big thank you to the original designer for creating such a fantastic model! I hope you enjoy exploring this epic build. A few notes about the digital model: Since I recreated this model before the official building instructions were available, I used a speed-build video as a reference to help complete the model. While I cannot guarantee that every single detail is identical to the original, I'm confident she is approximately 99% accurate. One small detail I couldn't get right in Stud.io is the attachment of the shrouds to their anchor points. Whenever I tried to attach them, Stud.io kept deleting them or moving them to completely different positions, so I eventually decided to leave them unattached in the digital model.
